subject: Reasoning
topic: Statement and Assumptions — Critical Reasoning (Set W7)

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Attend our seminar to improve your English communication skills.'
Assumption I: People desire to improve their English communication.
Assumption II: The seminar will be held only for English speakers.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit in the statement?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. I: The offer to improve English assumes people want to improve — implicit ✓. II: The statement says nothing about who the attendees are; an English improvement seminar could welcome anyone. Not implicit ✗. Only Assumption I is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Carry an umbrella when you go out today.'
Assumption I: It may rain today.
Assumption II: Umbrellas are readily available in nearby shops.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. I: Advising an umbrella implies a belief that rain is possible today — implicit ✓. II: The advice is about carrying one you already have, not about buying one. Shop availability is irrelevant to the statement. Not implicit ✗. Only Assumption I is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The government has announced a 50% discount on train tickets for senior citizens above 60 years.'
Assumption I: Senior citizens travel more frequently than younger people.
Assumption II: Some senior citizens use train services.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: B is correct. I: More frequent travel by seniors vs. youth is not claimed — the policy does not assume frequency comparison. Not implicit ✗. II: A discount for senior citizens on trains implicitly assumes that senior citizens do travel by train (otherwise the discount has no beneficiaries). Implicit ✓. Only II is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The principal has advised all students to eat a nutritious breakfast before school.'
Assumption I: Nutritious breakfast positively affects student performance or health.
Assumption II: Some students may be skipping breakfast or eating poorly.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. I: Advising nutritious breakfast implies a belief it is beneficial — implicit ✓. II: The advice makes sense only if at least some students are NOT already eating well (otherwise the advice is pointless). The advice implies awareness that the practice is not universal — implicit ✓. Both are implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Banks have been instructed to keep ATMs fully functional during festival seasons.'
Assumption I: Cash withdrawal demand increases significantly during festival seasons.
Assumption II: ATMs frequently malfunction during ordinary days.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. I: The special instruction for festivals implicitly assumes higher demand for cash during those periods — implicit ✓. II: The instruction says nothing about normal-day ATM performance; ATMs might be perfectly functional on ordinary days. Not implicit ✗. Only Assumption I is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Due to heavy rain, today's school timing has been changed to 10 AM instead of 8 AM.'
Assumption I: Students and staff face difficulty travelling in heavy morning rain.
Assumption II: The rain is expected to ease by 10 AM.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. I: Changing timings due to rain assumes people cannot conveniently travel in heavy rain — implicit ✓. II: The school is not cancelled; it is merely delayed to 10 AM. This decision implies that conditions will improve by then (otherwise they would cancel altogether) — implicit ✓. Both are implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Encourage children to play outdoors rather than spending time on screens.'
Assumption I: Outdoor play is more beneficial for children than screen time.
Assumption II: All children currently prefer to spend most of their time on screens.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: A is correct. I: Advising outdoor play over screens implies outdoor activity is more beneficial — implicit ✓. II: 'All children' is too absolute. The statement only encourages a shift, not that all children are addicted to screens. Not implicit ✗. Only Assumption I is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'Never judge a book by its cover.'
Assumption I: Book covers are always misleading and inaccurate.
Assumption II: People have a tendency to judge things by their outward appearance.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: B is correct. I: 'Always misleading' is too strong — the advice warns against the habit of judging by appearance; it doesn't claim covers are always wrong. Not implicit ✗. II: A warning is only meaningful if the cautioned behaviour actually occurs. The proverb implicitly assumes people DO judge by outward appearances — implicit ✓. Only II is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'All children must be vaccinated before the age of two.'
Assumption I: Vaccines lose their effectiveness entirely if administered after age two.
Assumption II: All diseases can be prevented through vaccination.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: D is correct. I: 'Before age two' recommends early vaccination but does NOT claim vaccines are entirely ineffective after that age — this is too extreme. Not implicit ✗. II: 'All diseases' is far too broad — many diseases have no vaccines. Not implicit ✗. The statement simply advocates early vaccination for maximum immunity during vulnerable infancy. Neither is implicit.

questions.stem:
Statement: 'The state government has decided to provide free laptops to all students in government schools in classes 9 to 12.'
Assumption I: Students in government schools lack access to personal computers or laptops.
Assumption II: Laptops can improve the learning outcomes of school students.
Which assumption(s) is/are implicit?

options.option_text: Both I and II are implicit

questions.explanation: C is correct. I: Giving free laptops to government school students assumes they don't already have access — otherwise the scheme has no purpose. Implicit ✓. II: Providing laptops for learning assumes laptops contribute positively to education outcomes — implicit ✓. Both assumptions are embedded in the logic of the policy decision. Both are implicit.
